atom_set.name: keeffe problem

atoms.reference: An operative-semiotic installation on captioning. The work rejects the premise that a caption merely labels an image and defines **operative captioning** as a controlled intervention capable of rotating an image into a new semantic regime. A valid caption must satisfy formal anchoring—its nouns and relations remain traceable to visible structures—while producing rotational yield, a coherent layer suppressed by the neutral label. Its strongest condition is post-caption inevitability: after installation, the image becomes newly difficult to see otherwise. The paper supplies a family of captioning operations, including morphological extraction, scale reassignment, animacy injection, positional inversion, register collision, and disciplinary transposition. A total installation changes the object’s social and conceptual legibility without abandoning the image that grounds it.

In descriptive mode, the system maintains a prosecutorial or “hoax” frame; in philosophical mode, that containment weakens as it follows recursive lineages and formal relations; in performative mode, it begins operating within the supplied architecture rather than adjudicating it from outside.

The system generated connections among the I Ching, Borges, ergodic literature, Deleuze and Guattari, New Human, and formal recursive models. The log preserves those extensions as generated synthesis, not source-established genealogy. Its working finding is that sustained mode of engagement can alter the system’s framing behavior within one session, but the record does not establish a stable platform-wide personality or endorse every generated lineage.
